overclaims: A forecast like this can only be settled by a decisive event: AGI reached by an LLM-based system, or AGI reached by something clearly different.
Benchmark results such as ARC-AGI-3 (March 2026), where top models scored under 1% while humans solved every task, show AGI is not widely seen as achieved.
Some executives have claimed AGI, but those claims are not broadly accepted.
Benchmark gaps or failures before AGI arrives do not settle the forecast; they only show AGI has not yet arrived.
It is context only: the forecast is about which paradigm reaches AGI, and that event has not happened.
Context sources are mostly secondary reporting on benchmark results.
checks.note: March benchmark results and one organizer's position do not establish October-wide consensus or categorical nonachievement. Executive claims appear only in an excluded source. One of two cited sources is primary, so 'mostly secondary' is inaccurate. The event-only rationale also omits the contract's alternative support route through expert consensus on impossibility.

overclaims: In 2023 a law firm also filed fake court cases that ChatGPT had made up.

checks.note: The legal example concerns submitted fabricated opinions and citations, not fabricated lawsuits being filed. The 3% hallucination rate appears in packet gaps but is not documented in the supplied evidence excerpts or context; 'scored' also obscures the metric. OpenAI said 'similar limitations,' not 'the same limits.' The agreed supported outcome and historical period are preserved.
